name: application-task-priority-badge
title: Task Priority Badge Set
description: Task priority badge with a consistent icon and color scale across Urgent/High/Medium/Low — the icon, color, and label are always selected together from a single typed priority prop.
useWhen: Labeling a task, ticket, or issue with an urgency level in a table row, card, or list.
You want the priority's icon, color, and text to always stay in sync — driven by one prop instead of copy-pasted markup per level.
A compact inline badge fits better than a full select or radio group for a read-only priority indicator.
avoidWhen: The value isn't a priority/urgency level — use the generic badges component for arbitrary labels instead.
Users need to change the priority inline — pair this with a select or dropdown menu rather than using it alone as an input.
You need more than four levels — extend the priorityConfig map rather than approximating extra levels with color alone.
responsiveBehavior: Each badge is an inline-flex element sized to its content; badges wrap naturally in a flex-wrap row at any width.
accessibility: Priority is conveyed by icon shape, color, and a text label together — never color alone.
The icon direction (up/down arrows for High/Low, triangle for Urgent) reinforces the ordinal ranking beyond color.
Each level's config bundles label + color + icon in one lookup, so a given priority can never render with a mismatched icon or color.

variants.title: Task priority badge set
variants.description: All four priority levels (Urgent/High/Medium/Low) shown side by side, on a light surface.
accessibility: Each badge's icon direction and shape are distinct, not just its color, so the scale is legible without color vision.

variants.title: Task priority badge set (Dark)
variants.description: All four priority levels, adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Badge background and text colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark backgrounds.
